title: Diabetes mellitus: type, complications and medication status
question: Assign the ICD-10-CM codes for the patient's diabetes, its complications and related long-term drug use.
note:
Chief Complaint
Routine follow-up for type 1 diabetes.

HPI
The patient presents for a routine follow-up visit. He reports feeling well with no acute complaints since the last visit. He continues to manage his type 1 diabetes mellitus with insulin injections as prescribed. He denies any recent changes in routine or symptoms. Examination reveals no signs of complications related to his type 1 diabetes mellitus.

Medication List
Insulin regimen as prescribed.

Exam
Vitals are stable. Cardiovascular and pulmonary exams are unremarkable. Skin exam shows no signs of breakdown or acute changes. No evidence of complications noted on exam.

Assessment
The patient has a history of type 1 diabetes mellitus, managed long-term with insulin, and presents today with no complications.

Plan
Continue current insulin regimen. Follow up as scheduled. Patient instructed to monitor blood glucose as usual.
explanations: No complication documented: type 1 diabetes without complications.
Do not assign Z79.4 for type 1 diabetes; insulin use is inherent.

distractors.why: No hyperglycemia or poor control is documented.
Z79.4 is not assigned for type 1 diabetes.
